messages.author: 5712068fdf482d27
messages.subject: The behaviour of "shiny-busy"
parts:
It looks that the shiny-busy is not added to the html tag when the computation happens within an observe.

Can shiny-busy be added to it even when the code is run within observe({})?

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: The behaviour of "shiny-busy"
parts:
Possibly. The problem is that observe() is not formally tied to any specific session (which makes sense, as it's possible to have observers that run outside of any one session). However, I have a couple of ideas to deal with this problem:

1) Provide a formal link between an observer and a session, i.e. observe({...}, session=session). (Or possibly make the link implicit, i.e. we "know" what session you're running in.) This would nicely solve another issue we have, which is that when a session ends, you usually want any observers it created to be suspended.

2) Inside an observer, provide a hint about what related reactives or outputs are going to be invalidated by the side-effects of the observer. This would nicely solve another issue we have, which is that when an observer does lengthy calculations that eventually write reactive values, during the lengthy calculations the outputs that will eventually affected don't have the semi-transparent appearance (which we'll update to make look nicer at some point).
